description: Per-SINTRAN-user index for the old ND-500(0) domain format, mapping domain names to their :PSEG/:DSEG/:LINK files and bookkeeping.

verification.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-11, extended 2026-08-17: the DOMAIN entry is now code-proven too. Segment-entry AND domain-entry field offsets confirmed from the ND-500 Monitor's own code (MON-DEBUG:PROG J04), which reads this file and prints each field beside its own label, AND matched against real DESC files (segment fields against six real entries from three product installs; domain fields against all 13 sample files). Sizes are stored as size-1 (last byte index). The bytes 74-84 conflict is adjudicated in the manual's favour: they are the COMSEGSIZE and N100SEGNO arrays, bounded by COMSEGNO at byte 62 - the earlier 'two counted byte strings' reading was a misread loop idiom. The MEANINGS of dlinkdate/absfixad/lowlogfix/plologfix/puplogfix are only the monitor's printed labels - all five read zero in all real entries.
fileSources: NLL H02 installer floppy 210319H02-XX-01D: description-file.desc (22528 bytes), with linkage-load-h02.pseg (123989) and .dseg (2184977) beside it
LED floppy 211160B03-XX-01D: description-file.desc (22528 bytes), with led-b03.pseg (223695) and .dseg (394525) beside it

COBOL-85 K01 floppy 210177K01-XX-01D: description-file.desc (22528 bytes), with cobol-85-k01.pseg (265213) and .dseg (129253) beside it - found 2026-08-17, after the offsets were fixed, so it is an independent check rather than a source
A second byte-identical copy of the COBOL K01 file exists as DESCRIPTION-FILE.DESC in a separate directory; it is the same witness, not a fourth install

structure.domainEntryPosition: position = 56*index + 256*(index div 32 + 1); first entry at byte 256
structure.segmentEntries: singly linked list: domainEntry.seglink = file byte position of the first segment entry; segmentEntry.seglink = position of the next; 0 ends the chain
structure.note: Verified in all four real DESC files: domain entries at 0x100 and 0x138, chains -> 0x4000 and 0x40C0, each terminating with 0. The layout is identical across the three product installs.

fields.name: firstDomainNumber
fields.description: Domain number of the first domain belonging to this process.

domainEntry.verified: RESOLVED 2026-08-17: all offsets code-proven from the monitor's domain print routine (014035B-014520B), each label paired with its field load off buffer 037651B, and checked against all 13 sample DESC files

fields.name: seglink
fields.description: File byte position of this domain's FIRST segment entry (head of the segment linked list).

fields.name: dname
fields.description: Domain name, terminated by a 0x27 (apostrophe) byte not documented in the manual (same convention as segmentEntry.sname), then zero-padded to fill the field. Not visible in the first-checked sample (LINKAGE-LOAD-H02, exactly 16 chars, no room for a terminator) - confirmed 2026-08-10 via SCRATCH-DOMAIN (14 chars + terminator + 1 zero byte).

fields.name: childDomains
fields.description: Byte array of child-domain indexes; element count is childIndex (byte 27). Max 6 fit before mother at byte 26.
fields.evidence: 014407B AAT 12 + LBYT loop, label $Child domains   : ; count loaded from low byte of word 15B at 014375B

fields.name: mother
fields.description: Domain index of mother domain; 0xFF = no mother (all root domains in all 13 samples).

fields.name: childIndex
fields.description: Number of child domains (equivalently the first free slot in the child-domain area). The monitor prints it as 'Childindex:' and uses the same byte as the childDomains element count.

fields.name: flagPrior
fields.description: One 16-bit word, not the manual's separate procPrior/flag bytes: bit 15 'alton', bit 14 'dinuse' (set on every in-use entry in all 13 samples, clear on unused), bit 13 'occup'; bits 5-12 = priority (printed as '  Prior:'). Bits 0-4 unprinted, zero in all samples. The priority field spans the byte boundary, so the manual's byte split cannot be right.

fields.name: stadr
fields.description: Start address. 0 for SCRATCH-DOMAIN, segment-1 addresses (0x8000004 etc.) for real programs in the samples.

fields.name: enableint
fields.description: Bitmask of enabled traps.

fields.name: tha
fields.description: Trap handler address.

fields.name: sysenabl
fields.description: Bitmask of system-enabled traps.

fields.name: unprinted46
fields.description: Not printed by the monitor; zero in all 13 samples. The manual's field order has no room for it (its field list sums to 54 in a 56-byte entry - this word is the missing 2 bytes).

fields.name: pbitmap
fields.description: Monitor label '  PSEG use:'. Bitmap of used program segments, confirmed by two independent segment numbers: value 2 (bit 1) on entries with STADR in segment 1, and value 4194304 (bit 22) on LINKAGE-LOAD-H02 whose STADR 0xB0000DD1 is segment 22. NOTE: manual order suggested byte 46; the code-proven offset is 48.

fields.name: dbitmap
fields.description: Monitor label '  DSEG use:'. Same bitmap shape as pbitmap. Manual order suggested byte 50; code-proven offset is 52.

segmentEntry.verified: RESOLVED: seglink/sname byte-exact; plb/psize/dlb/dsize/debuginfo/dlinkdate/absfixad/lowlogfix/plologfix/puplogfix confirmed from the monitor's print routine and matched against real files

fields.name: seglink
fields.description: File byte position of the NEXT segment entry in this domain's chain; 0 = end of chain.

fields.name: sname
fields.description: (directory:user)filename, terminated by a 0x27 (apostrophe) byte not documented in the manual, then zero-padded to fill the field.

fields.name: segtype
fields.description: Flags indicating segment type.

fields.name: comsegno
fields.description: Number of shared (common) SINTRAN-III segments; bounds comsegaddr/comsegsize/n100segno/addsgelem, max 5. ADJUDICATED 2026-08-17: this word is NOT a character count - the monitor prints it under its own label '$Comsegno: ' and uses it to bound a word array and a double array as well, which no string reading explains.
fields.evidence: 015151B LDA ,X 37 printed after label at 040514B ('$Comsegno: '); count reloads at 015222B/015257B/015313B/015362B

fields.name: comsegaddr
fields.description: Array of 5 x uint16 (one WORD per common segment, not loose bytes): logical address of each shared SINTRAN-III segment within the data segment. Label '$Comsegaddr: '.
fields.evidence: 015233B AAX 40, word-indexed loop 015220B-015245B, elements printed as numbers

fields.name: comsegsize
fields.description: Byte array [5]: size of each shared segment. Label '$Comsegsize: '. Elements printed as NUMBERS via 013301B (library number converter wrapper), not as characters - the old 'counted byte string' reading is retracted.

fields.name: pad79
fields.description: Padding between the two byte arrays; never touched by the monitor.

fields.name: n100segno
fields.description: Byte array [5]: actual SINTRAN-III segment numbers. Label '$N100segno:  '. NOTE: manual order suggested byte 79; the code-proven offset is 80 (word 50B, word-aligned).

fields.name: plogDlogHddindex
fields.description: PLOG (5 bits, logical program-segment number), DLOG (5 bits, logical data-segment number), HDDINDEX (3 bits).
fields.liveDataPoint: CONVERT-DOM-A03 reported LINKAGE-LOAD-H02's logical segment as 22 during a real conversion run, 2026-08-10 - useful for cross-checking PLOG once the offset is pinned.

fields.name: plb
fields.description: Logical low bound for program segment.
fields.evidence: monitor prints label $PLB: then 014575B loads ,X 54B off the segment-entry buffer 037705B

fields.name: psize
fields.description: Program segment size, stored as size-1. Confirmed on 6/6 real entries across three product installs (NLL H02, LED B03, COBOL-85 K01), each checked against the real .pseg file beside the DESC.
fields.evidence: monitor prints label Psize: then 014610B loads ,X 56B off the segment-entry buffer 037705B
fields.encoding: size - 1 (last byte index, NOT a byte count)

fields.name: dlb
fields.description: Logical low bound for data segment.
fields.evidence: monitor prints label $DLB: then 014636B loads ,X 60B off the segment-entry buffer 037705B

fields.name: dsize
fields.description: Data segment size, stored as size-1. Confirmed on 6/6 real entries across three product installs. Correction 2026-08-11: LINKAGE-LOAD-H02's stored value is 2109142, not the 2109654/2109655 previously reported - that was an arithmetic error. Re-read byte-for-byte 2026-08-17 from the H02 floppy's description-file.desc at file offset 0x4124 (raw 00 20 2e d6); note that 0x4120 is DLB, not DSIZE - an earlier note cited the wrong offset for the right value.
fields.evidence: monitor prints label Dsize: then 014651B loads ,X 62B off the segment-entry buffer 037705B
fields.encoding: size - 1 (last byte index, NOT a byte count)

fields.name: debuginfo
fields.description: Size of debug info on the :LINK file.
fields.evidence: monitor prints label $Debuginfo: then 014677B loads ,X 64B off the segment-entry buffer 037705B

fields.name: dlinkdate
fields.description: Labelled 'Dlinkdate:' by the monitor and described by the manual as the date the segment was last linked. The OFFSET is proven; the MEANING is not. This field reads zero in all six real segment entries available, including shipped linked products (LINKAGE-LOAD-H02, LED-B03, COBOL-85-K01) where a link date should be set. Either NLL never writes it in a shipped domain, or the field is not a date at all.
fields.evidence: monitor prints label Dlinkdate: then 014712B loads ,X 66B off the segment-entry buffer 037705B

fields.name: absfixad
fields.description: Absolute fixed address, if fixed.
fields.evidence: monitor prints label Absfixad: then 014750B loads ,X 70B off the segment-entry buffer 037705B

fields.name: lowlogfix
fields.description: Lower page number in fixed area.
fields.evidence: monitor prints label $Lowlogfix: then 014763B loads ,X 71B off the segment-entry buffer 037705B

fields.name: upplogfix
fields.description: Upper page number in fixed area.

fields.name: minpages
fields.description: Minimum pages in memory.

fields.name: maxpages
fields.description: Maximum pages in memory.

fields.name: indiplogInddlog
fields.description: Bitfield word: Indplog = bits 10-15, Inddlog = bits 5-9 (monitor's labels '  Indplog: ' / '  Inddlog:  ') - logical program/data segment number in an indirect domain.

fields.name: addsgelem
fields.description: 5 elements x 12 bytes (6 words - multiply constant at 015553B), count = comsegno; fills the entry to exactly 192 bytes. Monitor label '$Addsgelem:  ' prints the first double of each element. Manual's per-element split (ADDSEGLINK(4) + INDDOMAIN(1) + bitfield + LINKDATE(4)) sums to 15 bytes and cannot fit 12 - the inner layout is NOT settled, only the element size and base.
fields.verified: base, element size, and count code-proven; inner field layout manual-order only and inconsistent with the 12-byte element
fields.evidence: 015372B MPY (constant 6 at 015553B), 015374B AAX 102, LDD ,X 0 per element

fields.name: plologfix
fields.description: Monitor's own label 'Plologfix:'. Not named in the manual.

fields.name: puplogfix
fields.description: Monitor's own label 'Puplogfix:'. Not named in the manual; likely the manual's UPPLOGFIX.

fields.name: flagsWord
fields.description: Flags word the monitor prints bit by bit (015743B-016052B); individual bit meanings not decoded.

fields.name: elink
fields.description: Link to next symbol.

fields.name: sl
fields.description: Length of symbol name.

fields.name: nleOper
fields.description: NLE (3 bits, numeric length) + OPER (operation type +,-,*,/).

fields.name: ident
fields.description: Language code.

fields.name: cw
fields.description: Type-of-symbol bitmask, see cwBits. Same layout as the NRF loader's in-memory symbol table (see nrf-format.json symbolTypeBits).

fields.name: val
fields.description: Value of symbol.

fields.name: size
fields.description: Size of common block.

fields.name: ss
fields.description: Symbol name.

cwBits.name: DREF
cwBits.description: false = program memory reference, true = data memory reference

cwBits.name: DSYM
cwBits.description: false = program label, true = data label

cwBits.name: GLOB
cwBits.description: true = symbol survives a loader-table save

cwBits.name: OMIT
cwBits.description: true = module must not be loaded

readPath.summary: The ND-500 Monitor does NOT use RFILE. It opens DESCRIPTION-FILE:DESC (descriptor build at 016200B-016240B), then seeks and reads bytes.
readPath.readDomainEntry: 013454B - computes position, reads 56 bytes into buffer 037651B
readPath.primitive: 013406B - MON 74 SETBT (seek to byte position) then a MON 1 INBT byte loop stored with SBYT
readPath.consequence: the buffer holds the raw record byte for byte, so word offset * 2 = file byte offset exactly

resolvedQuestions.description: Was reported as: LINKAGE-LOAD-H02 is the only entry with non-zero DLB (75834) and the only one whose DSIZE (2109655) does not match its .dseg file (2184977). Resolved 2026-08-11: the DSIZE-stored value used in that comparison (2109654/2109655) was a transcription error - re-reading description-file.desc offset 0x4124 gives raw bytes 00 20 2e d6 = 2109142 (0x4120 is DLB). With the correct value, DLB + (DSIZE_stored + 1) = 75834 + 2109143 = 2184977, exactly matching the .dseg file size - the same formula the zero-DLB entries already satisfy trivially. Not a format anomaly.

openQuestions.description: The size-1 encoding is proven from files and consistent with the monitor's own inclusive-last-index style (277B=191 for the 192-byte record, 67B=55 for the 56-byte entry), but the monitor never adjusts the values, so a write-side proof must come from NLL.

nonWitnesses.finding: Does not read these fields. Patching PSIZE from 123988 to 16384 in a real DESC and re-running the conversion under nd500x produced a byte-identical 2,316,049-byte .DOM; it queries the filesystem with MON 62B GetBytesInFile instead.
